author: NavyandGuts
quote:
GTA 6 represents everything I fear modern Rockstar has become, and a complete abandonment of the values that made this franchise legendary in the first place.

The original Grand Theft Auto games were built on irreverence, controversy, unapologetic satire, dark humour, and an absolute refusal to bow to social expectations. Rockstar wasn’t afraid to offend, provoke, mock institutions, expose hypocrisy, or push boundaries. That rebellious spirit was the very identity of GTA.

What made GTA special wasn’t simply its open world, graphics, or gameplay. It was its attitude. Its willingness to be politically incorrect, morally ambiguous, provocative, and downright outrageous. It was a satirical reflection of society that spared absolutely nobody.

Somewhere along the way, it feels like Rockstar has forgotten what made its own creation special. Instead of embracing the fearless creative identity that defined the franchise, modern GTA increasingly feels like a product designed to satisfy corporate expectations and avoid controversy.

I don’t want a sanitized version of Grand Theft Auto. I don’t want a game afraid of its own identity. I don’t want Rockstar trying to convince me how progressive, acceptable, or culturally relevant it can be.

I want the Rockstar that had the courage to make fun of everyone and everything, without discrimination or apologies.

GTA was never supposed to be comfortable. It was supposed to be outrageous.

And if Rockstar has abandoned that philosophy, then it hasn’t just changed the franchise. It has abandoned the very spirit that made it great.

I don’t miss the old graphics, mechanics, or technology. I miss the old Rockstar.
